what_it_does: Modern AI applications often need to search enormous collections of high-dimensional data vectors to find the closest matches — for example, finding the most relevant documents for a large language model to read before answering a question. Graph-based search algorithms are effective for this but, when the vector database is too large to fit in fast memory, the graph must live on a solid-state drive (SSD). Reading from an SSD is far slower than reading from chip memory, and naive access patterns leave most of the SSD's available bandwidth and computing potential idle. GraphAccel is a specialized processor embedded inside the SSD itself — a concept called in-storage computing — that reduces wasted bandwidth through two techniques: packing related graph nodes into the same storage pages so fewer reads are needed, and speculatively exploring multiple search paths in parallel to keep all parts of the SSD busy at once. This approach is compared against DiskANN, a well-known SSD-resident vector search system.
